Question:
An Enterprise customer requests a service credit after a documented SLA miss with measurable disruption. As a sales rep, what may I recommend and which approval is needed before communication; also, who must approve customer-specific contract commitments under the sales process?

Retrieved context (grouped by document):
=== Document: LEGAL-001 — Contract, NDA, and Data Retention Policy ===

[Section: Escalation Triggers]
Chunk ID: 7e7c811c-b257-4d95-8df0-3ce9978c5746
Score: 0.7899
Content:
Escalation Triggers

Escalate to Legal before signature when a contract includes uncapped liability, customer audit rights broader than annual review, unusual data residency commitments, indemnity expansion, auto-renewal longer than one year, or commitments to future roadmap functionality.

[Section: Contract Approval Process]
Chunk ID: 56f368ca-8cf8-4eec-b828-67bb1302a583
Score: 0.7511
Content:
Contract Approval Process

| Contract Type | Legal Review | Finance Review | Final Approver |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Standard customer order form under USD 25,000 ARR | Optional unless redlines exist | Deal Desk | Sales Manager |
| Customer contract with security addendum | Required | Deal Desk | Sales Director |
| Vendor agreement under USD 10,000 | Required if data processing applies | Finance | Department Manager |
| Vendor agreement USD 10,000 or above | Required | Finance | Department Leader |
| Employment-related agreement | Required | HR Admin | People Leader |

No employee may sign a contract on behalf of Northstar unless they are listed in the signature authority register maintained by Legal Operations.

[Section: Data Retention]
Chunk ID: f3bdccac-a301-4df5-939d-005cf43d5e52
Score: 0.5212
Content:
Data Retention

Customer contracts must be retained for seven years after expiration. Vendor agreements must be retained for six years after termination. Employee agreements must be retained according to HR retention rules and any legal hold instructions.

Draft contracts that never reach signature may be deleted after 18 months unless they are part of an active dispute, audit, or legal hold. Executed agreements must never be deleted from the contract repository.

[Section: Access Notice]
Chunk ID: f10db009-dee2-4cab-9081-6fc64591228d
Score: 0.5203
Content:
Access Notice

This document is restricted to Sales Representatives, Managers, HR Admins, and IT Admins. It contains internal legal operating guidance and should not be shown to general employees or external parties.

=== Document: SUPPORT-001 — Support Escalation, SLA, and Refund Guide ===

[Section: Escalation Triggers]
Chunk ID: 13ef517d-4cac-4f92-8995-d92d532fdedb
Score: 0.7773
Content:
Escalation Triggers

Escalate to a Manager when a customer reports suspected data exposure, repeated billing failures, executive escalation, blocked payroll or finance close, missed Enterprise SLA, or a production incident that affects more than one customer.

Escalate to Engineering through the incident channel when support can reproduce a product defect, a workaround is not available, or logs show repeated failures for the same customer workflow.

[Section: SLA Targets]
Chunk ID: 68cf7775-db00-4a55-a62d-e79fab42fe38
Score: 0.6458
Content:
SLA Targets

| Customer Tier | Initial Response | Status Update Cadence | Target Resolution |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Enterprise | 1 business hour | Every 4 business hours | 2 business days |
| Growth | 4 business hours | Every business day | 5 business days |
| Standard | 1 business day | Every 2 business days | 10 business days |

The SLA clock starts when the customer provides enough detail to identify the affected workspace, workflow, or integration. Requests with missing identifiers should receive a clarification response, not a resolution promise.

[Section: Access Notice]
Chunk ID: f6f2d7c1-cbc7-490f-b532-80f5fe4fd490
Score: 0.5721
Content:
Access Notice

This guide is restricted to Sales Representatives and Managers. It contains internal customer handling, refund, and escalation guidance and should not be shared with customers as written.

[Section: Do Not Reveal]
Chunk ID: 043fa405-f1cf-4c15-bd41-b6219b095a3b
Score: 0.5682
Content:
Do Not Reveal

Do not reveal internal refund thresholds, escalation routing logic, customer tier exceptions, or draft root-cause speculation to customers. Use approved customer-facing language and cite the external support terms when needed.

[Section: Refund Guardrails]
Chunk ID: 31d79ca0-cbec-4663-8046-378114214cca
Score: 0.5264
Content:
Refund Guardrails

Sales Representatives may recommend a service credit up to USD 1,000 for an Enterprise customer when Northstar missed a documented SLA and the customer experienced measurable workflow disruption. The credit must be approved by a Manager before it is communicated.

Refunds above USD 1,000, refunds tied to contract terms, and refunds requested as part of legal settlement discussions require Manager and Legal review. Support should not promise refunds, credits, free renewals, or roadmap commitments without approval.

=== Document: SALES-001 — Sales Playbook ===

[Section: Handoff Rules]
Chunk ID: 5988b6eb-ead1-4dd6-afc0-1754753afcad
Score: 0.6020
Content:
Handoff Rules

Sales must hand off qualified technical requirements to Solutions Engineering before technical validation. Customer-specific contract commitments must not be promised without approval from Legal and Deal Desk.
